item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact Upload API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption, and verifies multipart replay. A introduces prohibited APIs and unrelated retry machinery while failing the required signature and delegation design.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead accepts ...UploadFileOption, breaking the frozen API contract.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field name \"file\" and delegates Upload and Add to one response/request path. A adds NewFileWithFields and independently duplicates Add's request construction and response decoding instead of routing through Add.","A explicitly adds association-field options and WithFileFormField, despite the contract prohibiting association fields, and changes the return types of existing option constructors.","A makes broad, unrelated changes to RawClient retry/body ownership semantics, including suppressing closure of seekable bodies and mutating ContentLength/GetBody behavior. The contract explicitly excludes retry-machinery refactoring and requires only the Upload-produced body to be replayable patientistically via the established helper pattern. B's localized buffering is easier to review despite changing Add internals. B's Upload test verifies field name, filename, content, and successful replay after 429 on both attempts."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong public option type and existing FilesOption values are no longer generally accepted.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating its option processing, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error logic.","Prohibited association APIs and multipart helper machinery significantly expand scope and maintenance burden. The generic seeker-based GetBody closure returns the same mutable reader for every replay and changes body-closing semantics globally. Tests do not visibly cover source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the new private add helper rather than literally calling the existing public Add method, so it does not strictly satisfy the required routing formulation.","Add now eagerly buffers every custom body, altering its prior streaming behavior and memory profile despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","The visible tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases, relying on multipartbody.NewFile for those semantics."]}
